answer: A market can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, with the stake slashed when peers prove fraud. Like a trellis that only lets one vine through each opening, the stake makes every extra identity pay full price, so creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes. Reputation then grows only from attested, completed work, a quiet whisper of past reliability rather than a loud claim, and newcomers start at the wharf edge of trust, earning larger deals only after a record of honest deliveries.
